Prepare a fitted emulator for PDE-free calibration

Source: R/calibration_prepare.R
calibration_prepare.Rd

Fits a Gaussian process (the design GP) to the recorded autoregressive design matrices, so that design rows can be predicted at untried inputs. Reuses the fitted emulator's coefficient samples or draws additional samples from saved filtering results, without refitting the dynamic emulator.

Usage

calibration_prepare(
  emulator,
  lower,
  upper,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = 1234,
  sampling = NULL,
  design_uncertainty = TRUE,
  design_kernel = c("matern52", "sqexp"),
  design_groups = c("time", "shared")
)

Arguments

emulator

A sigma2R object from emulator_learn().

lower, upper

Finite parameter bounds in training-column order. Equal bounds specify fixed coordinates. Named bounds are matched to the training parameter names.

n_draws

Number of fresh coefficient sample sets. NULL reuses existing samples when the selected sampling method agrees with the fitted emulator.

seed

Optional local seed used when drawing fresh samples.

sampling

NULL inherits the fitted emulator's method (normally "marginal"). "marginal" draws independent smoothed episode coefficients conditional on a shared variance; "joint" draws coherent backward paths. Changing the method resamples the existing number of draws unless n_draws is supplied.

design_uncertainty

If TRUE (the default), the predictive covariance of the AR design GP is added to the field covariance used by calibration_fit() and calibration_predict(). FALSE uses the GP mean only, as spDBL 1.1.1 did; its intervals are too narrow.

design_kernel

Kernel of the design GP: "matern52" (Matern 5/2, the default) or "sqexp" (squared exponential). Both are anisotropic, with one lengthscale per free parameter on the unit scale.

design_groups

"time" (the default) fits separate kernel hyperparameters, by maximum likelihood, for the design columns of each time step; "shared" fits one set for all times. design_kernel = "sqexp", design_groups = "shared" reproduces the design GP of earlier spDBL versions.

Value

A spDBL_calibration_input object containing the training data, coefficient samples, offline design predictor, and shared GP factors. At most one draw's residual weights are cached at a time.

Details

The AR design GP supplies the design rows at a new input. At each time step, all design columns share one kernel (with design_groups = "time"; one kernel for all times with "shared"), so their prediction errors at an input \(\eta\) are jointly Gaussian with covariance \(C_{F,t}(\eta) = v_t(\eta)\hat\Sigma_{F,t}\): \(v_t(\eta)\) is the GP's latent variance factor and \(\hat\Sigma_{F,t}\) is the maximum-likelihood covariance between the design columns of time \(t\). With design_uncertainty = TRUE this is propagated through each coefficient draw: at each time, the field covariance gains \(\Theta^\top C_{F,t}(\eta) \Theta\) over the episodes of that time, including covariance between spatial blocks. Design errors are treated as independent across times and independent of the emulator's own prediction error. The emulator's conditional covariance and coefficient uncertainty are always retained. Calibration support is limited to the scalar sigma2R model on the original time/grid. Objects prepared by spDBL 1.1.1 or earlier have no design variance.

See also

calibration_validate(), calibration_fit(), emulator_predict()

Examples

data("dt_calibration")
d <- dt_calibration
steps <- 1:6  # the first 6 of 26 time steps, to keep the example fast
em <- emulator_learn(d$training$input, d$training$responses[steps], d$Nx, d$Ny,
                     covariance = "sigma2R", episode_window = 2, nsam = 3,
                     seed = 1)
cal <- calibration_prepare(em, d$lower, d$upper)
class(cal)
#> [1] "spDBL_calibration_input"      "offline_calibration_emulator"
c(times = cal$T, locations = cal$S, draws = cal$M)
#>     times locations     draws 
#>         6        36         3 
cal$parameter_names
#> [1] "eta1"   "eta2"   "alpha1" "alpha2" "alpha3"
